title: Stage 5 — Relational Databases (SQL)
goal: Replace in-memory storage with SQLite — inspect rows with CLI/GUI and prove data survives restarts.
summary: Tables, primary keys, timestamps, parameterized SQL. Persistence before the UI connects.

pages.title: Why data must outlive the process

checkpoint.prompt: curl POST returns 201 but GET returns an empty list. SELECT * FROM workouts shows the row. What's wrong?

choices.text: GET handler reads from the wrong source — DB has data, handler doesn't query it
SQLite cannot store rows
created_at column blocks SELECT

checkpoint.explanation: Direct SQL confirms the row exists. If GET is empty, the handler isn't reading the DB.

choices.text: A unique identifier for each row
The password for the database
The first column you add alphabetically

checkpoint.explanation: Primary keys let you reference one specific record reliably.

checkpoint.prompt: SQL to read every column from table `workouts`.
checkpoint.explanation: `SELECT * FROM workouts` returns all columns and rows.

checkpoint.prompt: Why use `?` placeholders instead of string concatenation in SQL?

choices.text: Prevents SQL injection from malicious input
Makes queries run slower on purpose
SQLite forbids INSERT without ?

checkpoint.explanation: Never build SQL with template strings from user input.

checkpoint.prompt: After swapping to SQLite, you restart the API. curl GET still returns data. What changed?

choices.text: Data is stored on disk, not only in RAM
Express caches everything in the browser
GET requests now create data

checkpoint.explanation: The database file persists across process restarts.

checklist.label: GET/POST use SQL instead of in-memory array
INSERT uses `?` placeholders, not string concat
Verified writes with SELECT in CLI or GUI
Schema and swap committed with clear message

questions.prompt: Why run SELECT in sqlite3 after curl POST?

choices.text: Confirms the row actually landed in the database file
SELECT is required before every curl command
It replaces the need for GET /workouts

questions.explanation: Direct SQL inspection catches INSERT bugs curl status codes can hide.

questions.prompt: POST /workouts maps to which SQL operation?

choices.text: INSERT
SELECT
DROP TABLE

questions.explanation: Create → INSERT. Read → SELECT. Update → UPDATE. Delete → DELETE.

choices.text: Single file, zero setup, real SQL
It only works in production
It replaces the need for an API

questions.explanation: SQLite is a real relational DB in a file — perfect for learning.

choices.text: Records when each row was created without extra INSERT code
It makes the primary key auto-increment
SQLite requires timestamps on every table

questions.explanation: Database defaults set created_at automatically on INSERT.

questions.prompt: What does `NOT NULL` on a column mean?

choices.text: Every row must have a value for that column
The column is hidden from SELECT
Only nulls are allowed

questions.explanation: The database rejects rows missing required fields.
